prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1159; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving two vehicles. The insured's driver is named on the policy, and the claimant reports a shoulder injury and is represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the incident. Witnesses named in the report confirm the claimant was present.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the described impact. Some details are visible, though no independent witness has come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 4: Requested the vehicle's repair estimate and prior damage history. Nothing in the history suggests earlier damage, and the coverage period was already in force on the loss date with no sign of prior damage before it started.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's representative, who confirmed the claimant's account of the collision. The claimant described the event the same way as in the first notice.

Entry 6: Received the initial medical records. Treatment for the shoulder followed a typical course, and the provider noted that symptoms were gradually easing.

Entry 7: Checked for any prior claims or medical history involving the same shoulder. No earlier injury to that area is on record.

Entry 8: Follow-up call with the claimant. The account matched the earlier statements in every detail, with no changes to the timeline or the sequence of events.

Entry 9: Reviewed the updated treatment notes. Therapy visits have reduced in frequency as the claimant improves, and the provider has not yet linked the current condition clearly to this incident.

Entry 10: Discussed the file with the claims supervisor. Causation of the shoulder injury remains unclear, and the medical question is still open pending further records.

Entry 11: Requested an independent medical review and will hold the bodily injury evaluation until the reviewer's findings are received. Next step is to update the representative on the timeline.
